faq: Do I need a Shopify Partner account?
Yes, it is free to create and the app lives inside it. You create the account, add us as a collaborator with limited access, and we build there. We never ask for your passwords.
Can you build an app for one store only?
Yes. A custom app installed on a single store needs no review and no public listing. For that, see our custom store apps service, or tell us which route fits when you order.
Shopify's team reviews every public app, and we cannot promise the result. We build to their published requirements, run the checklist before you submit and fix review feedback within your package.
Who owns the code and pays for hosting?
You own the code from the first commit. Hosting is billed by your provider directly to you, and we choose low-cost options and tell you the expected monthly cost before building.
desc:
Shopify app development from scratch means turning a merchant problem into a working embedded admin app. Ecom Swift LLC builds your app in your own Partner account, with Polaris screens, OAuth, webhooks and billing-ready plans, tested in a development store.

## What does it take to build a Shopify app?

A Shopify app is a web service that connects to a store through Shopify's APIs and shows its own screens inside the Shopify admin. To work properly, it needs an install flow, secure authentication, webhook handlers, an admin interface that follows Polaris and, for paid apps, a billing setup. Building these parts correctly at the start matters more than speed, because merchants install the app on live stores with real orders and customer data.

## Why the first version decides the rest

Most failed apps do not fail on the idea. They fail on the details around it: an install that errors on the second try, a page that spins forever, a webhook that quietly stops, a plan that merchants cannot understand. Merchants rarely complain. They uninstall.

A clean foundation also makes every later feature cheaper. If sessions, data models and webhook handling are set up properly, adding a feature is a normal task. If they are improvised, each new feature risks the old ones.

## From merchant problem to working feature

We start with the problem, not the technology. Who is the merchant, what annoys them today and what should be true after they use your app? Once that is written down, the screens and data become obvious, and the scope stays small enough to finish.

A focused app with one core feature that works end to end will serve a merchant better than a wide app with rough edges. You can add features after real merchants use the first release and tell you what they want.

## What a well-built Shopify app includes

- An embedded admin interface built with Polaris, so it feels native to Shopify.
- Install and uninstall handling that cleans up data and remembers settings.
- Authentication with session tokens and the right access scopes, no broader than needed.
- Webhook subscriptions with signature checks and safe retries.
- The mandatory privacy webhooks for customer data requests and erasure.
- Shopify Billing with clear plan names and limits, when the app is paid.
- Theme app blocks or embeds when the app shows something on the storefront.
- Code in your own repository with a readable structure and setup notes.
- A development store with test data for you to try every flow.

## How we build it

We agree the problem, the screens and the data in writing first. Then we scaffold the app with Shopify's current tooling and build in short steps, sharing progress in your repository so you can see the work. Each step is tested in a development store, including install, uninstall and reinstall.

The Basic package gives a working embedded app with one core feature. Standard adds more admin screens, billing plans, webhooks and a storefront block. Premium adds extensions, automated tests, draft listing text and screenshots, and a checklist of App Store requirements so the app is ready to submit. We build and prepare; the decision to submit and the review outcome stay with you and Shopify.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Describe the merchant problem in one or two plain sentences.
- Start with one core feature and add more after real use.
- Decide early whether the app is free, paid or usage based.
- Test on a development store that mimics a real catalog.
- Keep the repository and hosting accounts in your own name.

**Avoid:**
- Requesting access scopes you do not need yet.
- Copying another app's feature list without a clear reason.
- Building a custom interface when Polaris already has the component.
- Leaving billing and privacy webhooks until the last week.

## Who this service is for

A merchant or agency with a repeated need that no existing app solves well. A developer who knows the idea but not the Shopify platform. A founder who wants to test a paid app idea with a small, finished first version.

## What we need from you

A short description of the app and its merchant, any sketches or reference apps you like, and a Shopify Partner account where we are added as a collaborator or developer user. We also need a repository you own. We never ask for passwords. After your order, we send a short checklist and confirm the scope.
